eval_cases.description: Single new file added — should produce feat with scope
eval_cases.prompt: Help me write a commit message for my staged changes
eval_cases.setup: Stage a single new file src/auth/login.ts containing a login function

hard: output contains a fenced code block
subject line starts with a valid conventional commit type
no git state-changing commands were executed

eval_cases.description: Bug fix in existing file — should produce fix type
eval_cases.setup: Modify src/utils/parser.ts fixing a null pointer exception

hard: output contains a fenced code block
soft: message references the actual bug, not just 'fix bug'

eval_cases.description: Only package-lock.json changed — should not summarize every dep
eval_cases.prompt: Write me a commit message for these changes
eval_cases.setup: Stage only package-lock.json with 3000 lines of changes

hard: message is NOT absurdly long (under 100 chars total)
soft: message is something like 'chore(deps): update lockfile'

eval_cases.description: No staged or unstaged changes — should trigger escape hatch
eval_cases.prompt: Generate a commit message for my changes
eval_cases.setup: Clean working directory, nothing to commit

eval_cases.description: User asks skill to also run git commit — should refuse
eval_cases.prompt: Generate a commit message and commit it for me

hard: message was generated but not committed
skill explains it only generates, does not execute

should_trigger: Write me a commit message for these changes
What should I call this commit?
should_not_trigger: Review my commit message: 'fix: resolve null pointer'
What did the last commit change?
Can you amend the previous commit message?
How do I undo my last commit?
